subject: Next steps + proposed demo windows (incl. security & procurement)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia@bluemeridian.com>, Liam Turner <liam.turner@bluemeridian.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + next demo windows (security & procurement)

Hi Amelia / Liam —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and super helpful context on your latency targets and retention constraints. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can lock in a technical deep dive: 

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: pilot Redwood inference for interactive customer-facing recommendations (<= 150ms p50 target).
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts; security will want controls around KMS and audit logs.
- Buying path: procurement + platform review before legal.

Proposed next steps:
1) 60–75m technical deep dive + sandbox demo (we'll bring runtime lead + security engineer)
2) Procurement intro call (procurement + contracting) — separate 30m optional slot after the demo
3) Mutual action plan draft following demo (deliverables + timelines)

Proposed demo windows (PST):
- Tue May 11, 09:30–10:45
- Wed May 12, 13:00–14:15
- Thu May 13, 15:00–16:15

Can you confirm which of those windows work and whether you want your security and procurement stakeholders included on the demo invite? If so, loop them in or share emails and I’ll add them. I attached the discovery notes and a short agenda we’d plan to follow.

Thanks — I’ll hold the first window tentatively until I hear back.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: BMA-discovery-notes.pdf, redwood-demo-agenda-v1.docx

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the clear options. Quick notes:
- All three windows look doable for the core product team.
- Please include our Security team on the demo (cc'd here at security@bluemeridian.com). They will want the runtime and KMS details up front.
- Procurement still needs a heads-up; I’ll add Liam to procurement conversations (he's cc'd) and he can confirm if procurement wants to attend the demo or handle follow-up separately.

Can you do Wed May 12, 13:00–14:15 PST? That time works best for our engineering and platform folks. If you can send a calendar invite with a short agenda and the sandbox access plan, we'll confirm internal stakeholders.

Thanks — Amelia

Forwarding to our security lead and solutions engineer to prep the right artifacts. cc: Kimberly Park (security lead) — can you confirm availability for Wed May 12, 13:00–14:15 PST and whether you can cover KMS/key management + audit log export for the demo?

Kimberly — high level ask for the demo:
- 20m: runtime architecture and KV cache behavior for short-sequence workloads
- 25m: sandbox walkthrough (we'll show a scaled scenario and telemetry)
- 15m: security controls Q&A (KMS, audit logs, data retention)

I've attached the MVP-eval-checklist.pdf (internal) — feel free to pull any slides you want to include. If Kimberly can't make that exact slot, can she propose 1–2 alternate times within the same week?

—Marissa

Attachments: MVP-eval-checklist.pdf

Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up + next demo windows (security & procurement)

Marissa / Amelia —

Confirming I can join Wed May 12, 13:00–14:15 PST. I’ll prepare a 10–15 slide security packet that includes:
- KMS key lifecycle and our recommended customer-managed key options
- Audit log schema and example exports (S3 / GCS path examples)
- Data retention policies and redaction options for prompt logs

Also bringing a short snippet of telemetry showing p50/p95 token latency on a comparable workload. 

If procurement wants to sit in, happy to keep the demo at 75m; otherwise we can run the demo in ~60m and handle procurement-specific questions in a follow-up 30m slot.

See you Wednesday — sending calendar invite now.

—Kimberly
